newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-INTER STAY TOP AS VICENZA BLOW HISTORIC CHANCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTER STAY TOP AS VICENZA BLOW HISTORIC CHANCE.

text.p: Vicenza wasted a historic chance to go top of Serie A on Sunday when they drew 2-2 at lowly Verona to remain a point behind Italian leaders Internazionale.
Vicenza, who have never held the sole lead in Serie A, could have leapfrogged Inter at the top with a victory after the Milan club were held to a 2-2 home draw by Fiorentina on Saturday.

But Francesco Guidolin's side were lucky to come away with a point after an own-goal by captain Giovanni Lopez and a goal by Filippo Maniero gave their northeast Veneto rivals an early 2-0 lead in a hard-fought derby.
Striker Roberto Murgita cut the gap in the 36th minute and Verona defender Marco Baroni returned Lopez's favour with an own-goal 11 minutes from time.
Verona, Napoli and Udinese took to the pitch wearing black armbands in memory of their former goalkeeper Giuliano Giuliani, 38, who died of an AIDS-related illness this week.

Some 50,000 fans in Naples observed a minute's silence for him before their team's match against Perugia. Helped by two goals from Alfredo Aglietti, Napoli won 4-2 to move into joint fourth in the table with European champions Juventus.
The Turin club can join Inter at the top of the table later on Sunday, but will need to beat fellow giants AC Milan at home.
Bologna, meanwhile, knocked Juventus out of third spot as Swedish and Russian internationals Kennet Andersson and Igor Kolyvanov both scored in a 3-1 comeback victory against bottom club Reggiana.

Colombia's Adolfo Valencia had put unlucky Reggiana on top with a right-footed blast in the 42nd minute but Bologna drew level five minutes after halftime when Andersson netted from the ground after slipping.
Kolyvanov's 78th-minute penalty made it 3-1 after defender Michele Paramatti had given Bologna the lead in the 69th.
At Genoa, Italy striker Enrico Chiesa equalised with seven minutes left to give Parma a 1-1 draw over Sampdoria in his first match against his former club, who sold him last May.
"It's still 'work in progress'," Chiesa said of Parma, who are struggling with just 12 points from nine matches.

It was also Parma's first match without Gianfranco Zola, who made his debut for English side Chelsea on Saturday, while it could be Christian Karembeu's last game for Sampdoria. The Frenchman is tipped to move to Barcelona or Real Madrid.

Sampdoria are four points adrift from Inter in joint fifth with Roma, who won 3-1 at home over former coach Carlo Mazzone's Cagliari. Roma's Argentina Abel Balbo struck twice to become Serie A's top scorer with eight goals.
Giuseppe Signori, whose missed penalty condemned Lazio to a 1-0 defeat at Napoli in a midweek Italian Cup tie, pulled off a hat-trick including a penalty to give the Rome side a 3-1 win at Piacenza.
At Bergamo, Atalanta exploited a 20th-minute own-goal by defender Valerio Bertotto to surprise Udinese with a 1-0 win vital to the northern club's hopes of avoiding relegation.
